content.text:
Fixed. **61/61 passing.**

## The bug

`1 lb 11.5 oz` is one size, but the parser took the first unit it found and stopped — reading `1 lb` and throwing the `11.5 oz` away. That understated the package and inflated the price per ounce:

| | true | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stone Oven, `1 lb 11.5 oz`, $7.99 | 27.5 oz | 16 oz → $0.50/oz | **$0.29/oz ← best value** |
| Pepperoni, `24 oz`, $8.49 | 24 oz | $0.35/oz | $0.35/oz |
| Thin Crust, `1 lb 4.6 oz`, $6.99 | 20.6 oz | 16 oz → $0.44/oz | $0.34/oz |

Pepperoni was the only one of the three parsed correctly, so it won by default.

## The fix

A new `extendCompound` in `src/parse.js` walks forward from a measured match and absorbs continuation parts.

    if (next.unit.family === base.unit.family) absorb(next);

Changes are uncommitted. Say the word and I'll commit.
